We found that there were four different areas where sanitary sewer manholes and or pipe were exposed to the stream and presumed to be because of that event, some erosion that had occurred. So we had had some initial discussions, made initial requests, and they have deemed those areas eligible for funding and have allotted funding for that. And in order to move forward with that, we of course have a variety of paperwork agreements that will need to be signed. And this legislation here will authorize the mayor to enter into those agreements that are necessary for us to receive that funding. And I think it was noted, I don't know if it was noted, but as of now, from the numbers I've been given, they are estimating that the cost of the improvements will be in the range of 172,000. and they do cover 75% of that. The way this assistance works is we as the city would have to put up the money upfront, pay for that cost, and then we submit for reimbursement thereafter. And again, they would cover about 75% of that, which is 129,000, give or take, and we would be on the hook for the remaining 43,000. I do have an email into NRCS that they have not answered at this point in terms of what happens if the bids come in higher than that estimate, or we have change orders that increase the cost. So I'm still waiting to hear word from them on that as to what those specifics are. But again, that's generally what we're looking at here. And I'm happy to answer any questions that anybody might have, if there's anything additional.

blocks.speaker: SPEAKER_12
blocks.text: Questions for Steven? I have a question, Mr. Chair. Yes. Now is this the 75% match or the reimbursement, is this guaranteed or is there a chance that the reimbursement application could be denied?

blocks.speaker: SPEAKER_11

That allotment, we were informed of that in February, which would put the deadline by September. Now, in the discussions I've had with my local NRCS contact who I've been working with on this, he says it is very common for local agencies to receive extensions to that. And from the impressions I've been given, it seems like they're generally understanding that these projects take time, especially in this case, we're dealing with permits through the Army Corps of Engineers, environmental issues. It's gonna be during Indiana bat season, so we may have to delay to get out of the season for that endangered species to avoid any issues there. So we're dealing with some environmental issues and in general, I'm told that they are understanding and it is common for extensions to be given, but my local guy did say, he can't say it's not up to him, of course, he can't say with 100% certainty that it might not be denied at some point in the future again likely it wouldn't be but again i certainly can't sit here and say that that that's not a possibility at least i think it's a small chance from what's been given to me but it's it's a non-zero chance is my understanding
